extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners (KIPO) and patent applicants/attorneys filing or prosecuting priority claims in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for formality and substantive examination of patent priority claims (Paris Convention / PCT and domestic priority) including requirements for legitimacy, timelines for amendment/withdrawal, evidential document submission, and rules for multiple and special-case priorities (e.g., US CIP/provisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid priority claims based on hypothetical/unspecified applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant filed an application claiming a priority under the Treaty based on a hypothetical application, an application filed by another entity or an application which cannot be specified, the applicant shall not be able to amend or add a priority claim since the priority claim is basically invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such priority claims are treated as invalid; after filing they cannot be amended/added. Examiner should treat as invalid when the first application cannot be specified or is not legitimately the applicant's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal/invalidity/finality on ability to amend/add priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim under the Treaty has been withdrawn or invalidated, where an application claiming for priority under the Treaty has been invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned, where a decision to grant/reject an application for a patent made by the examiner becomes final and conclusive, the applicant shall not be able to amend or add the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of a priority claim made on the same date on which withdrawal of all priority claims is made shall be accepted. The timing when decisions become final is specified (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality timing for grant/reject decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The time at which the decision to grant a patent becomes final and conclusive is when a certified copy of the decision to grant a patent is served to the applicant. The time at which the decision to reject an application becomes final and conclusive is when thirty days have elapsed from the date on which a certified copy of the decision to reject a patent is served to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must use these timings to determine whether subsequent amendment or addition of priority claims is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: One year and four months amendment/addition window
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, withdrawal of all priority claims, withdrawal of part of priority claims in multiple priority claims, amendment for correcting clerical errors in priority claims and amendment of adding priority claims shall be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawal/addition is to be made within this period, applicant need not separately submit a withdrawal document and may submit an amendment reflecting withdrawal/addition. The statutory period cannot be extended beyond 1 year 4 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post 1 year 4 months limitation to clerical corrections only
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments of a priority claim after one year and four months has elapsed shall be permitted only when correcting clerical errors in the indication of the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the first application, specifying a first application not previously specified, or adding the first application after this period are not allowed. Withdrawal of all or part of priority claims remains allowed even after this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination prerequisite to substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an application claiming priority under the Treaty or a written amendment to priority claim is submitted, the examiner shall examine the formalities of priority claim based on the patent application or the written amendment. Unless any deficiency is found in priority claim, the examiner shall carry out the substantive examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formality deficiencies exist, examiner requests amendment; failure to address deficiencies within designated period allows examiner to invalidate proceedings for the priority claim and treat the application as a normal application without priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination requirements for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements for formality examination on priority claim under the Treaty include: the identicalness of the applicants, the earliest filing date of the first application filed in one of the countries under the Treaty, the regularity of the first application, the compliance with the priority period, the description of the purport of priority claim and the submission of the evidential documents proving the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must check each listed element when assessing formality; deficiencies in part of multiple priority claims may lead to partial invalidation (see Note1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deficiencies in multiple priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where deficiencies are identified in part of multiple priority claims, the examiner shall request the applicant to amend only priority claims containing deficiencies. If applicant does not address the deficiencies within the designated period, the examiner shall invalidate priority claims whose deficiencies were not addressed, other than invalidating all priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial invalidation is allowed; examiner should avoid invalidating unproblematic priority claims unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Patent Net / WIPO records for evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidential documents certifying the priority in an international patent application can be checked through the evidential documents for priority claims posted onto the Patent Net. If not available, examiner can access attached documents via WIPO (http://www.wipo.int/pctdb/en). If still not confirmed, examiner shall request amendment and then determine whether to invalidate priority claim after considering submissions and opportunity to explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should exhaust electronic sources before requesting applicant submission; provide opportunity to explain before invalidating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of invalidated priority claim for substantive examination date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner has invalidated priority claim since the claim is illegitimate based on the result of the formality examination and amendment to priority claim, the examiner shall examine the application ... based on the filing date of the application with a priority claim under the Treaty (the filing date in the Republic of Korea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation of priority shifts applicable prior art cutoff and patentability determination to the local filing date rather than any earlier priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting retroactive filing date by invention when priority legitimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority claim is found to be legitimate, the examiner shall determine whether to grant a retroactive filing date by invention when examining the patentability of the inventions. For inventions identical to those in the first application (specification/drawings), examine based on filing date of the first application; otherwise examine based on filing date of the claiming application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may request translations of evidential documents to compare content. When delivering grounds for rejection without retroactive filing date, examiner must describe why the retroactive date was not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identicalness standard for retroactive priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for identicalness do not mean claims must be identical; rather the invention described in the claims of the application claiming priority shall be identical to the invention in the specification or drawings of the first application. Determination uses the standard in Article 29(3) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Article 29(3) standard; identity may be by invention (not necessarily claim language). Examples illustrate partial identity (e.g., subsets of compounds/elements take priority date for those subsets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where inventions deemed identical (priority by invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions described in first application and claiming application deemed identical in cases such as: (i) claiming part of the first application; (ii) two or more claiming apps based on divisional apps of the first app; (iii) a single claiming app filed based on more than two first applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: even when an invention excluded from the first application is described in the claiming app, priority can be acknowledged for inventions included in the first application — i.e., priority can be acknowledged by invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple priority claims (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications including more than two priority claims (multiple priority claims), the examiner shall not reject the priority claim simply because it was filed based on two or more first applications. However, where inventions are not recognized to be identical, the examiner can notify grounds for rejection (Article 45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may divide the application; after division each application can enjoy priority benefit. Examiner must assess each invention's applicable priority date (see further sub-rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of priority dates for multiple-first-application cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Korean patent application has priority claims for more than two first applications, the examiner shall examine the application based on the earliest filing date of each invention under the Treaty in accordance with Articles 29 and 36 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an invention is based on one of the first applications, examine based on filing date of that first application. If an invention combines subject matter separately described in different first applications (e.g., a+b where a only in A and b only in B), examine that combined invention based on the filing date of the Korean application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawing earliest-filed priority among multiple claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim in the first application having the earliest filing date has been withdrawn among more than two priority claims, the filing date of the earliest-filed remaining application shall be deemed to be the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must determine whether the newly earliest-filed application meets requirements to serve as basis of priority claim under the Paris Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: General instruction: accept evidential documents issued by other patent offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries have various types of patent application systems; each patent office can determine whether their applications are regular national applications seeking priority claim and then issue evidential documents. Other patent offices can recognize priority based on those evidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO examiners should rely on evidential documents issued by other offices as indicators of legitimacy, subject to further verification where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of priority claims based on US Continuation-In-Part (CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority claim is based only on a US CIP and only the CIP specification was submitted as evidential documents, examiner shall examine inventions based on the date to determine patentability without granting retroactive filing date. If original application spec/drawings are submitted, follow the guideline for original/CIP combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invention is described only in CIP, CIP filing date used. If invention described in both original and CIP and claiming app filed within one year of original, subject matter in both takes original filing date; subject matter only in CIP takes CIP filing date. If claiming app filed after one year from original, retroactive date may not be available for subject matter described in original and CIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIP exception to being 'first application' under Paris Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: CIP application is not recognized as the first application prescribed in Article 4C(2) of the Paris Convention; therefore, in principle a CIP's priority claim cannot be recognized. Exception: if a copy of the original application's specification/drawings (including application number) has been submitted and the claiming application is ensured to be claiming priority based on subject matter only in the CIP spec/drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must confirm presence of original spec/drawings with application number to consider exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of priority claims based on US provisional and non-provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications and converted provisional/non-provisional relationships affect which application can serve as basis for priority claim. Examiner shall determine legality based on which application the USPTO has issued evidential documents for; the priority period starts on filing date of the provisional recognized as the filing date of the legitimate application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally, if non-provisional not filed after provisional, provisional serves as basis. If non-provisional filed claiming benefit of provisional, the provisional serves as basic application and priority period begins on provisional's filing date. Examiner relies on USPTO-issued evidential docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to submit evidential documents within 1 year 4 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidential documents certifying priority under the Treaty are not submitted within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, the concerned priority claim shall lose its effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall request amendment and invalidate the priority claim procedure; procedural error cannot be addressed (documents returned if submitted after the statutory period). For national stage entries, the examiner grants opportunity to submit evidential documents after national stage and accepts them if submitted in response to amendment request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic exchange / streamlined procedure handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority claim is based on first application submitted to a country with streamlined procedure for submission of evidential documents and application number is filed, examiner shall check whether KIPO could be offered the evidential documents through electronic exchange (except JPO/EPO). If record of exchange within submission period cannot be checked, examiner shall request amendments and invalidate the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle late-submitted or exchanged evidential documents after designated period lose effect per Article 54(6); exception where applicant completed legitimate procedures for exchange in both countries, examiner may regard late submission/exchange as legitimate and recognize the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory nature of the 1 year 4 month period
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed for amendment or addition of priority claim according to Article 54(7) of the Patent Act is statutory and it cannot be extended after one year and four months. Even if a request for amendment was made within the period, amendments such as addition of priority claim cannot be accepted when one year and four months has elapsed from the earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner can describe the purport of refusing amendments or addition of a priority claim in the written request for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim eligibility (Article 55 conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may claim domestic priority based on an earlier patent or utility model application on which he/she is entitled: provided that (1) the relevant patent application is filed within one year of the prior-filed application, (2) the prior-filed application is not a divisional/converted application in disallowed circumstances, (3) the prior-filed application is not abandoned/invalidated/withdrawn at time of filing, (4) no final/conclusive decision on grant/reject/utility registration has occurred before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must state intention and indicate the prior-filed application in the patent application. If requirements met and invention identical to prior-filed original spec/drawings, application deemed filed at the time of prior-filed application (retroactive date) per relevant Articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority amendment/addition window
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who claims domestic priority which meets requirements may amend or add the priority claim within one year and four months from the filing date of the prior-filed application (referring to earliest filing date if multiple prior-filed applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the Treaty-based priority amendment window; statutory periods apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application deemed withdrawn at 1 year 3 months (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application to which priority is claimed shall be deemed withdrawn at the time one year and three months have elapsed from the filing date of the prior-filed application, except where certain exceptions apply (e.g., prior-filed app abandoned, final decision, priority claim withdrawn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No applicant shall withdraw the priority claim upon expiration of 1 year 3 months. If the patent application claiming priority is withdrawn within 1 year 3 months, the priority claim is deemed withdrawn simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purport of domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority claim is designed to ensure protection for an invention developed based on a prior-filed application to further specify, improve or add to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority allows inventions identical to those disclosed in prior-filed application to be treated as filed on the earlier date, while newly added improvements are treated as filed on the claiming application's date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can make a domestic priority claim is the applicant of the prior-filed application (including a successor in title under Article 38(4) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both applicants of prior-filed and claiming applications must be considered for identicalness/entitlement; successor-in-title recognition included.
